nodes.label: Provenance Chain (SourceDocument to Opportunity)
nodes.rationale: Claim was the missing entity; makes 'where did this come from' a click-through answer instead of stopping at the signal.

nodes.label: Agent Runtime Contract (Section 10.1a)
nodes.rationale: Bounds max_iterations/max_tool_calls/max_runtime_seconds/max_results/max_tokens so an agent cannot become an unbounded tool-call loop; hitting a limit returns truncated:true instead of failing the run.

nodes.label: Evidence Diversity Check
nodes.rationale: Renamed from 'triangulation' to be honest that it measures source diversity, not independence; underlying_event_risk left unknown on purpose.

nodes.label: Eligibility Gate (Section 0.1)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed 17 Sept 2026, present in no prior PRD version; a hard entry gate checked directly against the rules page.

nodes.label: Repo History DQ Rule
nodes.rationale: Single highest-severity compliance item; a repository whose history doesn't match event dates disqualifies the whole team.

nodes.label: AWS Use Must Be Visible in Video
Agents Discover, Code Verifies, Humans Decide
nodes.rationale: The product principle: research agents propose signals never opportunities; a deterministic gate decides what's allowed; a human decides what to send.

nodes.label: No Composite Opportunity Score
nodes.rationale: A weighted-sum score had an arithmetic bug and conceptually hid two different questions (confidence vs attractiveness) behind one number; removed in favor of three separately-shown values.

nodes.label: Opportunity Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Pain + strength is a correlation, not automatically an opportunity; a stated, gate-checked mechanism is required to bridge evidence to commercial rationale.

nodes.label: Observed/Inferred/Assumed Labeling (Section 13.3)
nodes.rationale: One label system generalised across every claim so a viewer can tell at a glance what kind of claim they're looking at.

nodes.label: Data Acquisition Risk: Live to Cached to Demo Fixture Ladder
nodes.rationale: Tavily/web extraction is the PRD's top named technical risk; a three-level fallback labels the UI honestly rather than silently substituting data.

nodes.label: Outreach Policy (Section 18.1)
nodes.rationale: An opportunity can be built on a public complaint, but outreach must never let the recipient feel surveilled.

nodes.label: Sample-Business Policy (Section 3.3)
nodes.rationale: PulseStack is simulated but its named competitors are real; no simulated claim is ever attributed to a real company.

nodes.label: Vertical-Agnostic Reasoning Engine Principle (Section 3.1)
nodes.rationale: The reasoning engine is vertical-agnostic; playbooks adapt evidence sources, opportunity types and economics to each business - defensible in a way 'works for any business' is not.

nodes.label: Fix-First Rule (Section 9.3)
nodes.rationale: Opportunity isn't just about finding demand - it's about knowing whether you're ready to capture it.
